title: Proxy scenario factory for SDK backoff and stream sanity tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable proxy scenario factory that can generate deterministic, parameterized traffic fixtures for Python/TypeScript/Go SDK contract tests and VCR recording. The goal is a small, extensible harness that can synthesize streaming sessions with controlled backpressure, mid-stream resets, partial-chunk delays, idempotency markers, and server-side injected errors so SDKs can exercise retry/backoff logic and streaming ergonomics deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: Factory can emit at least 6 scenario primitives: chunk_delay, chunk_size_variation, abrupt_reset, server_500_after_n_bytes, kv_cache_warm_prefix, and slow_initial_response
Recorded VCR artifacts produced from the factory are byte-identical across runs given the same seed
Python/TS/Go SDK test suites can replay factory fixtures and assert retry path taken (e.g., attempted retries == expected, final error vs success)
Streaming tests validate SDK buffer semantics: partial frames surface to user callback, reassembly occurs correctly after retry, and user-provided cancelation hooks are honored
Fixtures stored in repo under testing/fixtures/sdk-fixtures with clear schema and a playback CLI
qa_plan: Run cross-language contract runner on CI with 3 random seeds + seed=42 deterministic run. Compare checksums of VCR outputs.
Introduce a synthetic network flakiness toggle in CI matrix to validate live proxy vs recorded playback parity
Manual post-merge: exercise a Canary pipeline that replays fixtures against staging Redwood API to detect regression in runtime behavior
Performance sanity: ensure playback harness adds <5% overhead to existing suite wall-clock time when cached fixtures are used
updates: 2025-01-10 - Ticket created by Aisha. Drafted goals and initial API surface for the factory. Suggested primitives and seed-based determinism.
2025-01-13 - Spike complete: PoC proxy implemented as small Node service that rewrites chunk boundaries and injects delays. Recorded sample VCR for a streaming chat session (seed=7).

2025-01-15 - Review with SDK leads (Sophie, Marco): agreed to keep the playback format newline-delimited JSON events instead of binary cassettes to ease diffs; downside is larger fixture size—acceptable tradeoff for readability.
2025-01-17 - Feedback from Security: ensure no real API keys are captured in fixtures. Update PoC to scrub authorization headers and replace with placeholder tokens during recording.
2025-01-19 - Implemented deterministic seeding and checksum verification in prototype. Added helper to 'fast-forward' KV-cache warm prefix to simulate cache hits for prefix-based paths.

2025-01-21 - PR opened for playback CLI and fixture schema with basic Python/TS/Go adapters (see PoC PR). Running cross-lang runner locally — observed flakiness in Go SDK reconnection timing; assigned follow-up to ENG-56007.
2025-01-22 - Decision: adopt NDJSON schema for fixtures + metadata header containing seed and generator version. Next: add test matrix entries and productionize playback runner in CI.
notes: Trade-offs: NDJSON is human-readable but larger; binary cassette format would be compact but harder to inspect. Chose NDJSON for onboarding speed and debuggability.
We must not record PII or auth tokens; scrub at capture time and fail recording if sensitive headers are present.
Consider future extension: a 'scenario composer' UI to let non-devs craft regression reproductions from incident sessions.
Edge case: when simulating partial-chunk delivery for models with function-calling or structured output, ensure token boundaries are preserved so schema validators can run against assembled output.
